newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Novosibirsk telecom sees capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Novosibirsk telecom sees capital increase.

text.p: Shareholders of Russian telecoms company Novosibirskaya Telefonnaya Set (NGTS) will vote on March 28 whether to increase authorised capital, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

The Novosibirsk telephone company is planning to raise its capital to 500 million roubles from 80 million through a bonus issue and redenomination of shares, while revaluing assets, said Vera Belosludtseva, deputy chief executive for economic issues.
Controlling shareholder AO Svyazinvest, with 50.66 percent of shares, had instigated the move, which would not raise fresh funds, she said.
New shares would be created and distributed among current shareholders in proportion to current ownership.
Share nominal value would be raised to 100 roubles from 40 roubles and new shares would also be created.
The issue is intended to fulfil a Russian Communications Ministry order to regional telecoms to increase authorised capital to reflect real value of the companies
Salomon Bros owns 21 percent of NGTS shares, CS First Boston owns 14 percent and Bashkreditbank owns four percent.
Svyazinvest is a government-controlled telecom holding company.
Belosludtseva said the company had scrapped earlier plans to increase authorised capital to 200.3 million roubles.
NGTS 1995 pretax profit rose to 16.38 billion roubles on 4.85 billion in 1994. Results for 1996 have not yet been released.
